principles.text: When indices gap down into support and individual names are stronger than the indices, opening-range-breakout entries have higher odds — the bounce raises the win rate, especially on relatively strong names.

On straight-up moves where price never touches the 9 EMA, a supplementary entry is to buy any day and stop at the low of day; in such runs each low of day stays above the prior day's low (seen on CRWD/Intel), so a stop-at-LOD survives.

Define and tighten your stop before entering — the biggest influence from Kristjan: set the stop at the low of day (~3%), and tighten over years (7-8% to 1%) alongside improving entry skills so you're not chasing extended names.

Think in percentages of account (and R-multiples), never absolute dollars; obsessing over dollar P&L is what stops traders from scaling up. To grow a small account fast, ignore the dollar size and focus on percentage/R per trade.
Trading is reacting, not predicting: you can never know the bottom; just react when a stock pulls back into one or (better) multiple support levels for a higher chance it holds and continues.

Prefer liquid, fast-moving, orderly names with the right theme; favor beaten-down names that remain liquid (>100-200M daily dollar volume even after 90%+ declines), as liquidity through the decline signals two-sided interest and more explosive bounces.
